findings.claim: 'The Three Poisons - greed (pig), hatred (snake) and delusion (cockerel) - are depicted at the centre of the Wheel of Life (Bhavachakra)', repeated in the body paragraph and in flashcard 11 ('Pig (greed), snake (hatred), cockerel (delusion).').
findings.truth: In the hub of the Wheel of Life the pig stands for ignorance or delusion, the snake for aversion or hatred, and the bird or cockerel for attachment or greed. Pig and cockerel are swapped in all three places. The Wheel of Life is named content in this section, so a student repeating the pairing loses the mark.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Bhavachakra: 'The pig stands for ignorance...'; 'The snake represents aversion or anger...'; 'The bird represents attachment'. Spec 2D 1.4 names the Three Poisons and the Wheel of Life.

findings.claim: Knowledge check 2 asks 'Which named source contains the Five Precepts (pancha sila)?' and keys the answer to the Khuddakapatha; practice question 4 offers the model source sentence 'The Khuddakapatha contains the Five Precepts as a foundation for ethical kamma'; the exam tip lists 'the Khuddakapatha (for the Five Precepts)'.
findings.truth: The Khuddakapatha holds the Going for Refuge, the Ten Training Rules, the Mangala and Ratana Suttas and the Nidhi Kanda on merit - not a Five Precepts passage. The spec names it, together with Dhammapada 181-187, under kamma, merit and rebirth. The knowledge check stem is re-pointed at kamma and merit so the key stays correct; the model source sentence now states what the text actually teaches.
findings.evidence: accesstoinsight.org Khuddakapatha contents (Khp 1-9); spec 2D 1.8: 'kamma, including Dhammapada 181-187 and the Khuddakapatha, merit and rebirth'.

findings.claim: 'The Dhammapada 1-2 affirms that the mind shapes all actions: "Mind is the forerunner of all actions"', with flashcard 12 repeating 'mind is the forerunner of all actions'.
findings.truth: Dhammapada 1 reads 'Mind precedes all mental states. Mind is their chief; they are all mind-wrought.' The verse is about mental states (dhamma), not actions, and the quotation marks make the wrong wording look verbatim. Dhammapada 1-2 is the named text for chanting in this section.
findings.evidence: accesstoinsight.org Dhammapada ch.1 vv.1-2 (Buddharakkhita); spec 2D 2.2 names Dhammapada 1-2.

findings.claim: All four lessons set the 12-mark part as 'Discuss this statement' with the type label '12 marks - Discuss a Statement', and the exam tips and two content panels refer to 'the 12-mark Discuss question' (lessons 1, 2, 3 and 4).
findings.truth: The command words used across this qualification are State, Outline, Describe, Explain and Evaluate. The 12-mark part is an Evaluate question; Discuss is another board's wording. Fourteen edits change Discuss to Evaluate in the question text, the type label, the exam tips and the two content panels.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 3 Command Words (lines 4278-4340): Evaluate, 12 marks, AO2. The word 'Discuss' does not appear anywhere in the specification.

findings.claim: Every lesson sets a second question labelled '3 marks - Describe' ('Describe the teaching of paticca-samuppada', 'Describe the Threefold Way', 'Describe the Five Khandas', 'Describe how Buddhist puja is carried out in the vihara').
findings.truth: This paper sets two questions, each numbered (a) to (d): 3-mark Outline three, 4-mark Explain two, 5-mark Explain two with a reference to a source of wisdom or authority, and 12-mark Evaluate. There is no 3-mark Describe part - the command-word appendix puts Describe at 4 marks. Each is re-cast as an Outline three question at the same 3-mark tariff, with the key re-sized to one mark per point.
findings.evidence: spec pages 340-390 (Paper 2 assessment overview: 50 minutes, 51 marks, two questions (a)-(d)); spec lines 2717-2730 (assessment information); Appendix 3 Command Words.

findings.claim: 'Tanha fuels the Three Poisons: greed (lobha), hatred (dosa) and delusion (moha).'
findings.truth: The lesson's own key fact two paragraphs later says the Three Poisons 'represent the root causes of tanha (craving)'. The standard teaching runs that way round: the three unwholesome roots underlie craving. The body sentence reverses the causation and contradicts the key fact.
findings.evidence: internal contradiction with the lesson's key fact; spec 2D 1.4 places the Three Poisons under the Second Noble Truth as causes of suffering.

findings.claim: The glossary and the inline definition both define 'Triratna' as 'A Buddhist community centre used in the Triratna Buddhist Order (Western Buddhism)'.
findings.truth: Triratna is a Western Buddhist movement, the Triratna Buddhist Order, not a type of building. The spec lists Triratna alongside Theravada and Mahayana as a tradition whose places of worship are studied. A student who answers 'a Triratna is a community centre' has named the wrong kind of thing.
findings.evidence: spec 2D 2.4: 'temples, gompas, viharas and shrines in Theravada, Mahayana and Triratna Buddhism'.

findings.claim: Knowledge check 3 reads 'The _____ (Tibetan Book of the Dead) is read aloud to guide the dying person's consciousness...' and the keyed option is 'Tibetan Book of the Dead' - the stem gives its own answer.
findings.truth: The key is right, so nothing here is factually wrong, but the item tests nothing. Option A: change the parenthetical in the stem to '(Bardo Thodol)', which leaves the key valid and makes the item test the Tibetan name. Option B: leave it for the question-type relabel pass. Recommendation: option A - it is a one-string change and the item currently earns a free mark.
findings.ruling: Stem parenthetical changed to Bardo Thodol.

findings.claim: 'The Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta identifies three types: obvious physical and mental pain; the suffering caused by change; and the subtle suffering of conditioned existence itself.'
findings.truth: The three types of dukkha (pain, change, fabrication) are drawn from other suttas and the commentaries, not from the first sermon itself. The three types are correct and match the spec wording, so the only defect is the attribution. Not mark-affecting - no edit.
findings.evidence: spec 2D 1.3 lists 'the different types of suffering as pain, fabrication and change' under the First Noble Truth bullet that names the sutta.

findings.claim: The body says an Arahant 'will enter nibbana at death', while the glossary says an Arahant 'has achieved nibbana and will not be reborn after death'.
findings.truth: An arahant reaches nibbana in life; what happens at death is parinibbana. The glossary is right and the body is loose, but both would be credited. No edit.

findings.claim: The 5-mark key writes 'merit (punya)' - the Sanskrit form - in a unit that otherwise uses Pali throughout (kamma, nibbana, panna, sanna, anatta).
findings.truth: The Pali is punna. Both words are correct in their own language and the spec names merit in English only, so this is not mark-affecting. Left alone, consistent with the ruling on the same issue in the AQA Buddhism practices unit.
findings.evidence: transliteration comparison; spec 2D 1.8 names merit in English

findings.claim: The inline definition of the Kimsila Sutta says it emphasises 'reverent and learningful behaviour'.
findings.truth: 'Learningful' is not a word. The glossary entry for the same text words it correctly ('reverence and a desire to learn'). A wording defect only, so no edit in a fact-check pass; flag for the next copy pass.
findings.evidence: glossary entry for the same term in the same lesson

findings.claim: All four 12-mark keys use the band ladder 'Mastering (10-12) / Secure (7-9) / Developing (4-6) / Emerging (1-3)'.
findings.truth: These are house band names, not the board's, so no copyright rule is broken, but they are not the house standard (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band). Left for the band-ladder relabel pass rather than edited here.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list and house band vocabulary

summary: Four lessons checked, 13 findings, 37 edits. Two hard factual errors: the Wheel of Life hub animals are paired with the wrong poisons (pig and cockerel swapped) in three places, and the Khuddakapatha is named three times as the source of the Five Precepts when the spec names it for kamma and merit. Two exam-form errors run through every lesson: the 12-mark part is labelled Discuss rather than Evaluate, and each lesson sets a 3-mark Describe question, a part this paper does not have. The Buddha's life, the Four Noble Truths, the Eightfold Path and Threefold Way groupings, the Five Khandas, the Six Perfections, the meditation types, the death rites by tradition, the festival list by tradition and all 20 knowledge-check answer keys are correct.
